title.justification: The title clearly states the focus of the paper, which is on the role of ghost units in yielding biologically plausible backpropagation in deep neural networks.
title.quote: G HOST U NITS Y IELD B IOLOGICALLY P LAUSIBLE B ACKPROP IN D EEP N EURAL N ETWORKS

analysis.description: The paper introduces a model that uses ghost units to achieve biologically plausible backpropagation in deep neural networks. By cancelling feedback from the upper layers when no target signal is provided, the model approximates error gradients in a biologically plausible manner. The approach is tested on classification tasks and is compared to traditional backpropagation methods.

type.justification: The paper conducts empirical experiments using the MNIST dataset and compares the performance of the proposed models with biologically plausible updates to standard backpropagation.
type.quote: In conclusion, using (MB) dynamics, the neural network is able to quickly learn a classification task... on the MNIST classification tasks, with different architectures (number of neurons, number of layers) and proved that these networks were able to accomplish such tasks as well as with backpropagation.

name.justification: The paper addresses biologically plausible methods for backpropagation, making significant connections between deep learning and neuroscience.
name.quote: This work is a step towards apprehending the mechanics of learning and memory in the brain, but at the same time, it raises interesting perspectives for implementation of deep networks in neuromorphic hardware.

name.justification: The paper is focused on understanding and implementing biologically plausible credit assignment mechanisms in neural networks.
name.quote: In this paper, we introduce a model that relies on a new role for a neuronal inhibitory machinery, referred to as ghost units... This gives the network the capacity to perform credit assignment in a multilayer structure by simply following its dynamics and updating the weights according to local plasticity learning rules.

name.justification: The research applies deep learning models and techniques to perform tasks such as classification, indicating the relevance to the broader field of machine learning.
name.quote: Deep learning has been the focus of intense studies in the past decade and has become more and more efficient in solving diverse and complex tasks, that range from pattern recognition, to image generation, NLP (natural language processing) and many others.

name.justification: Model A is a proposed model in the paper that involves a 1-1 correspondence between pyramidal units and ghost units.
name.quote: Figure 1: Architecture for Model A (MA) network with 1-1 correspondence between ghost units and associated pyramidal units from the following layer.

is_contributed.justification: Model A is presented as a novel contribution in the paper to achieve biologically plausible backpropagation.
is_contributed.quote: In this work, a class of neural networks models was developed, that enables learning as would backpropagation but with local learning rules. The first one (MA) where each pyramidal unit has an associated ghost unit in the previous layer.

is_executed.justification: The model is empirically tested on MNIST dataset, indicating its execution during experiments.
is_executed.quote: (MA) performance on the MNIST task 1-layer and 2-layer (MA) networks compete with the state-of-the-art when using a multilayer perceptron trained with backpropagation.

is_compared.justification: Model A is compared to other models (e.g., classical backpropagation) in terms of performance on tasks like MNIST
is_compared.quote: We also realized 1-layer experiments... these networks were able to accomplish such tasks as well as with backpropagation.

name.justification: Model B is a proposed model in the paper that allows ghost units to replicate feedback dynamically without a 1-1 correspondence with pyramidal units.
name.quote: Model description We also developed a different class of models that we introduce in this section. In this model (MB), we do not make any hypothesis on the number of pyramidal units and ghost units.

is_contributed.justification: Model B is presented as a novel contribution in the paper with dynamically replicating ghost units.
is_contributed.quote: In the second model (MB), we consider fewer ghost units that dynamically learn to replicate the feedback from the pyramidal units at each different pattern presentation.

is_executed.quote: Output probabilities of the classification task can then be read from the output pyramidal cells as seen in Figure 4 (top).

is_compared.quote: In particular learning goes well as the training accuracy reach 0.9976 (top). This is correlated with the mean-squared error that goes down and tends to 0 (middle).
